---
title: "Combine Excel Files"
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

pacman::p_load(openxlsx2, install = FALSE)

conflicted::conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")
```

## Introduction

This document combines multiple Excel files into a single Excel file while preserving the sheet names, order, and formatting of each original file. The files to be combined are:

1. DMP403_cg_sites.xlsx
2. go_enrichment_results.xlsx
3. top2000_cg_sites.xlsx

## Combine Excel Files

```{r}
#| label: combine-excel

# Start timing
tic("Excel combination")

# Define the input Excel files in the order they should be processed
input_files <- c(
  here("extended_data/output/DMP403_cg_sites.xlsx"),
  here("extended_data/output/top2000_cg_sites.xlsx"),
  here("extended_data/output/go_enrichment_results.xlsx")
)

# Create a new workbook for the combined file
combined_wb <- wb_workbook() |>
  wb_set_bookview(window_height = 100000, window_width = 100000)

# Process each input file
for (file in input_files) {
  cat(glue("Processing file: {file}\n"))
  
  # Load the source workbook
  source_wb <- wb_load(file)
  
  # Get sheet names
  sheet_names <- wb_get_sheet_names(source_wb)
  
  # Clone each sheet to the combined workbook
  for (sheet_name in sheet_names) {
    cat(glue("  Cloning sheet: {sheet_name}\n"))
    
    # Clone the worksheet from source workbook to target workbook
    combined_wb <- wb_clone_worksheet(
      wb = combined_wb,
      old = sheet_name,
      new = sheet_name,
      from = source_wb
    )
  }
}

# Contents sheet.
#
# Alzheimer's & Dementia requires that "the legends/captions for each item must be
# within the same file as the item". Each sheet already opens with its own legend
# row, so this adds the index that ties those to the Data S numbers the manuscript
# cites, as the first sheet of the workbook.
#
# The entries are DERIVED from the legend row of each cloned sheet, never restated:
# a hand-kept list here would silently drift from the sheets the moment one is
# renumbered, and a wrong number in a supplementary index is invisible to every
# check that reads the manuscript source.
contents <-
  wb_get_sheet_names(combined_wb) |>
  purrr::map_chr(\(s) {
    legend <- wb_to_df(combined_wb, sheet = s, rows = 1, col_names = FALSE) |>
      unlist() |>
      as.character() |>
      purrr::detect(\(x) !is.na(x) & nzchar(x))
    legend %||% NA_character_
  }) |>
  tibble::enframe(name = NULL, value = "legend") |>
  mutate(
    sheet = wb_get_sheet_names(combined_wb),
    item  = str_extract(legend, "^Data S\\d+"),
    # Not "the first sentence": several legends contain a period inside a value
    # ("P value < 1.0 x 10-8") and the GO ones continue into a bulleted column
    # glossary, so a sentence split truncates mid-number. Take a fixed span and
    # cut it on a word boundary instead.
    title = legend |>
      str_remove("^Data S\\d+\\.\\s*") |>
      str_squish() |>
      str_trunc(280, ellipsis = "...")
  ) |>
  select(Item = item, Sheet = sheet, Description = title)

stopifnot(
  "every sheet must open with a `Data SN.` legend" = !any(is.na(contents$Item)),
  "Data S items must be numbered 1..n in sheet order" =
    identical(contents$Item, paste0("Data S", seq_len(nrow(contents))))
)

combined_wb <- combined_wb |>
  wb_add_worksheet("Contents") |>
  wb_add_data("Contents", contents) |>
  wb_set_col_widths("Contents", cols = 1:3, widths = c(12, 20, 110)) |>
  wb_set_order(c(length(wb_get_sheet_names(combined_wb)) + 1,
                 seq_along(wb_get_sheet_names(combined_wb))))

# Save the combined workbook
fs::dir_create(here("extended_data/output"))
output_file <- here("extended_data/output/suppl_data_all.xlsx")
combined_wb |> wb_save(output_file)

# End timing
toc()

cat(glue("Combined Excel file saved to: {output_file}\n"))
```

## Summary

This document has created a combined Excel workbook that includes all sheets from the following files (in order):
1. DMP403_cg_sites.xlsx
2. go_enrichment_results.xlsx
3. top2000_cg_sites.xlsx

The sheet names, order, and formatting have been preserved in the combined file using the `wb_clone_worksheet()` function, which properly handles all Excel elements including styles, merged cells, and formatting.
